 LIVE RADAR: Storms moving through the Valley, across AZ 
 Weather 
 MOST ACCURATE FORECAST: Flood Watches in effect through Halloween weekend
 Prev 
 Next 
 This Halloween weekend, we are tracking a storm system set to bring in rain, wind and cooler air to Arizona. 
 By: 
 Amber Sullins 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add ABC15 as a Google Preferred Source 
 PHOENIX — A big fall storm is impacting Arizona as we head into Halloween weekend. 
 Showers and thunderstorms are already impacting the Valley and we'll see chances for more throughout the evening. 
 A few storms could be strong to severe, with damaging winds and hail.
 Flood Watches are in effect Friday and late Saturday night through Sunday for much of Arizona, including the Phoenix metro area. 
 We’ll see a lull throughout the day on Saturday with only a few hit or miss showers. But, rain chances ramp back up late Saturday night, hopefully after most of the trick-or-treating wraps up.
 On Sunday, we're tracking more widespread, soaking rain across Arizona.
 So, with impacts to outdoor activities and the potential to see areas of flooding, Friday and Sunday are ABC15 Weather Action Days .
 Take action to stay safe in the storms. If you hear thunder, head inside. That means, lightning is near and it could be deadly. 
 The Valley could see 1 to 2 inches of rain through Sunday, with 2 to 3 inches in parts of the high country.
 We’ll also see chances for a few more showers early Monday, mainly in eastern Arizona, before the forecast dries back out.
 This storm will bring a big dose of cool air, too.
 Valley highs will be in the mid to upper 70s Friday and Saturday before falling into the low 70s on Sunday.
